title: MLP Project Guidelines
text:
The MLP Project is a rigorous, hands-on classical machine learning course centered around a Kaggle competition. It requires students to build an end-to-end ML pipeline from exploratory data analysis and preprocessing to feature engineering and model tuning using classical ML libraries.
This website serves as the central handbook for the project. It outlines the deadlines, mandatory milestones, evaluation formulas, and the two-stage Viva examination process required to successfully complete the course.

title: MLP Project Guidelines
text:
1. Is it mandatory to complete the MLP Project in the same term as the MLP theory course?
Answer: No, students may complete the MLP Project in a subsequent term. It is highly recommended to complete the MLP theory course prior to undertaking the project to acquire the requisite foundational knowledge. However, students opting to undertake the project in the same term must ensure familiarity with the concepts and techniques covered in the theory course to facilitate successful project completion.
2. How should I proceed if I am undertaking both the MLP theory course and the MLP Project concurrently, and the project milestones require concepts not yet covered in the theory lectures?
Answer: Students pursuing both courses concurrently must adopt a proactive approach and independently study the relevant theoretical concepts at an accelerated pace. The first seven weeks of the MLP theory course curriculum encompass the concepts necessary for completing the project milestones.

title: MLP Project Guidelines
text:
Viva Examination
7. Is it permissible to attempt the Viva examination prior to the MLP Project submission deadline?
Answer: Yes, students may attempt the Viva examination before the MLP Project deadline, provided they are thoroughly prepared for the assessment.
8. Am I allowed to make submissions after completing the Viva examination?
Answer: Yes, if the Viva examination is completed before the project deadline, students may continue to make submissions. However, no submission will be accepted or evaluated after the official deadline has passed.
9. Is it possible to submit the MLP Project in the current term and defer the Viva examination to the subsequent term?
Answer: No, both the MLP Project submission and the Viva examination must be completed within the same term. The problem statement will change in the following term, necessitating a repetition of the entire submission and evaluation process.
10. When are the Viva examinations scheduled to take place?
Answer: The Viva examinations are tentatively scheduled to commence during the second week of November. The precise dates and timeline will be communicated by the course team at the end of October.
11. What is the official process for qualifying for and attending the Viva examination?
Answer: The primary prerequisite for Viva examination eligibility is achieving the minimum cut-off score on the Kaggle leaderboard. Further instructions regarding the examination process will be issued by the course team at the end of October.

ImportantMandatory Reading



Disclaimer: This document serves as a quick reference checklist to help you track your progress. However, it does not replace the main guidelines. You are expected to read the complete Project Guidelines Document at least once to fully understand the evaluation formulas, strict timelines, and comprehensive rules. Ignorance of the full guidelines will not be accepted as an excuse for invalidation.


To successfully pass the project course, you must meet all evaluation criteria and follow the structured workflow. Please ensure you have completed all of the following mandatory steps. You can use this checklist to track your progress:
1. Successful Registration

Create an account on Kaggle if you do not already have one.
Join the competition link provided in the guidelines.
Name the notebook as per the naming convention (YourRollNo-notebook-2026t3).
Share the notebook with the admin collaborator (iitmbscs2008p) with “can view” access and keep it Private.
Build a baseline model and make a valid first submission through the registered notebook.

Submit your notebook link via the Registration Google Form before the deadline (Nov 1, 2026).

2. Milestone Submissions

Complete and submit at least 2 out of 5 project milestones via the Seek portal before their respective deadlines. (A milestone is only considered complete when you receive the email response copy).

3. Cross the Cut-off

Achieve the minimum required score to cross the cut-off threshold on the Kaggle Leaderboard before your specific term’s deadline.

4. Notebook Readiness (Level 1 Checklist)

Ensure your notebook meets all the minimum requirements outlined in the Level 1 Viva Checkpoints section of the project guidelines.

5. Clear the Level 1 Viva

Successfully appear for and pass the Level 1 Viva examination in your designated batch.
The Level 1 Viva will evaluate your notebook based on the Level 1 Viva Checkpoints, your understanding of the code and the underlying ML concepts, and your ability to code and debug in real-time.
If you fail the Level 1 Viva, you will be given a single reattempt if you have attempted in Batch 1. Failing the reattempt will require you to repeat the project in the next term.

6. Clear the Level 2 Viva

Successfully appear for the Level 2 Viva and score at least 25/50 marks in your designated batch.
Failing the Level 2 Viva will require you to repeat the project in the next term. There will be no reattempt for Level 2 Viva.

title: MLP Project Guidelines
text:
Invalidation of Project Submission
Your project submission will be strictly discarded, and you will fail the course (requiring you to repeat the project in the next term) if any of the following violations occur:

Registration & Access Violations

Incomplete Registration: Failing to successfully submit the Registration Google Form. Without this form, you are ineligible to complete the project or attempt the vivas.
Mismatched Notebooks: Submitting a different Kaggle notebook link in the Registration Form than the one you are actually using to make your submissions.
Revoked Access: Failing to maintain “can view” access for the admin (iitmbscs2008p) on your FinalNotebook until the end of the term.
Public Notebook: Making your Kaggle notebook public at any point. It must remain strictly private to avoid plagiarism risks.



Submission Violations

Direct File Uploads: Making submissions by explicitly uploading .csv, .zip, or any other file formats to Kaggle will make invalidate the project. Only submissions made directly from the executed FinalNotebook will be counted.
Insufficient Milestones: Submitting fewer than the mandatory minimum of 2 out of 5 project milestones.



Academic & Technical Violations

Plagiarism: Any instance of plagiarizing code, insights, or models from the internet, a fellow student, or external sources. (Note: Participate individually; this is not a group project).
Unauthorized Libraries: Using deep learning, prohibited machine learning frameworks or libraries such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, NLTK, Pickle, AutoML frameworks, spaCy, word2vec, or textblob.
External Data: Using any external data to train your model.
Off-Platform Execution: Evaluating based on locally run experiments or pre-trained models. All end-to-end work must be visible and executed within the Kaggle notebook.



Evaluation Failures

Missing Deadlines: Failing to cross the Kaggle Leaderboard score cut-off by your term’s designated deadline.
Missed or Failed Vivas: Not booking a slot/appearing for your viva in the designated batch, failing the Level 1 Viva (and its single reattempt), or scoring below 25/50 on the Level 2 Viva (which has no reattempt).

title: Guidelines
text:
Evaluation & Passing Criteria
To pass this project course, you must meet all four criteria:

Registration: The registration must be completed successfully by Nov 1, 2026.
Cutoff Score: The submission from the registered notebook must cross the score cutoff in the Kaggle Leaderboard before the deadline.
Level 1 Viva: Must be cleared in the designated batch. Students who do not clear in the first attempt will be given a chance to reattempt. Failing the reattempt requires repeating the project next term.
Level 2 Viva: Must be cleared in the designated batch by scoring at least 25/50 marks. Failing the Level 2 viva requires repeating the project next term. There will be no reattempt for Level 2 viva.


Total Score Calculation
The formula for computing the Total Score (out of 100) is: Final marks = NB + M + L + S + V
Where:

NB: Score of your notebook out of 10 marks (assigned by the viva examiner).
M: 5 marks awarded for successfully completing all milestones.
L: Marks based on Kaggle Leaderboard performance, scaled from 0 to 30.
\[L = 30 \times \frac{\text{Your best score} - \text{cutoff score}}{\text{Top leaderboard score} - \text{cutoff score}}\]
S: Marks based on the number of submissions, scaled from 0 to 5.
\[
S = \begin{cases}
5, & \text{if public score is in top 20\% of leaderboard} \\
0, & \text{if } N < 10 \\
5 \times \frac{N - 10}{N_{\max} - 10}, & \text{if } N \ge 10
\end{cases}
\]
(Where \(N\) is the number of submissions made, and \(N_{\max}\) is the maximum number of submissions made as per the leaderboard).
V: Marks in Viva Voce, out of 50 marks.

title: Guidelines
text:
Level 1 Viva
The Level-1 Viva is designed to ensure that each participant in the Kaggle Project has put in a significant amount of effort in their MLP Project. This ensures that only participants who have shown dedication and effort in their Project work are eligible for the Level-2 Viva.






Important



Completing all items on the checklist is mandatory.



Level 1 Viva Checklist
The following components will be tested in the Level 1 viva:

Problem statement and dataset

The problem statement is understood correctly.
The dataset is appropriately loaded.

End-to-end analytical reasoning

The focus throughout the notebook from EDA → Preprocessing → Feature Engineering → Model Building → Error / Performance Analysis is to highlight the insights and explain the influence of each step on the subsequent approach.

Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Objective: Understand key statistics and relationships in the dataset.
Includes univariate and bivariate feature analysis on the relevant features.
Use appropriate visualizations that are clear, readable, and relevant.

Systematic preprocessing of the data

Detection and appropriate handling of missing values.
Need for appropriate scaling of numerical features.
Need for appropriate encoding of categorical features.
All data transformations (data cleaning, scaling, encoding, etc.) should be implemented using reusable pipelines or custom functions and consistently applied to both training and test datasets to avoid data leakage, ensure reproducibility, and reduce redundant code.

Feature Engineering / Extraction

Creation of new features / transformation of existing features followed by analysis of their importance.

Model experimentation and hyperparameter tuning

Experiment with multiple models from different families followed by hyperparameter tuning to optimize performance.

Model comparison

Compare the performance of at least three different models on training / validation data using appropriate evaluation metrics.
Highlight the advantages and disadvantages of each model.

Notebook quality

The notebook should be clean, well-structured, appropriately commented, and contain the relevant output.

Best-performing model

The notebook submission should contain the best-performing model.








Note



The Level-1 viva serves as a check to see if minimum requirements are met before attempting Level-2. The final scores will depend only on the Level-2 performance.

title: Guidelines
text:
Repeat L1 Viva
If a student does not meet the minimum requirements in the Level-1 viva, they will get another chance to clear the Level-1 viva provided it is attempted in Batch 1.

Level 2 Viva Preparation

Explain your code: Be prepared to provide an in-depth explanation of your code, including the reasoning behind your choices and the logic implemented as requested by the examiner.
Conceptual Knowledge: Examiners may ask questions from any DS diploma course you’ve taken (MLF, MLT, statistics, etc.), not just the specific project domain.
Internal Mechanics: Using an API is not enough. You must understand the 5 components of any used model: Data, Model, Loss function, Optimization, and Evaluation.
Live Coding: You may be asked to write code from scratch or modify your existing code during the exam.

text:
Submission Instructions






ImportantFormatting and Submission Rules



Please read and follow these instructions carefully. Strict adherence to the formatting and naming conventions is required to ensure your submission is processed correctly by the automated grading pipeline.



Document Preparation

Create a copy of the provided .docx template for the current milestone.
Write your answers directly beneath each of the 10 questions in the document.

Answering Guidelines

Length Constraint: Keep your answers concise. Provide no more than 10 lines of text per question.
Content Focus: For every question, you must clearly describe the specific classical machine learning approach you have taken and the underlying reasoning for your decisions. Focus on the why and how.

File Naming and Export

Once you have finished writing your report, save or export the .docx document as a PDF.
Rename the PDF file using the following exact convention: [roll-number]_26t3_M[Milestone-Number].pdf
Example: If your roll number is 21f1001234 and you are submitting the PDF for Milestone 1, your file must be named exactly: 21f1001234_26t3_M1.pdf








WarningNote on Evaluation



Failure to follow the exact file naming convention may result in parsing errors during evaluation. Please double-check your file name before uploading.
